blurb: Sixteen free, interactive Fanout Labs — small browser tools that make an inference, system-design, or ML calculation tangible instead of abstract.

adaptedFrom.name: Fanout (Suraj Gaud)
adaptedFrom.note: Fanout publishes no open licence on its site; Sikhi University has Fanout's written permission to link this directory. Every lab runs at fanout.sh — none of its code or interface is reproduced here. Unlike the rest of Fanout's catalogue, all sixteen Labs are free with no account required.

modules.title: Systems and inference labs
modules.objective: Turn eight abstract inference and systems-engineering ideas — capacity planning, KV-cache memory, GPU memory budgets, timeouts, latency, tokenization, sampling, and model cost — into something you can drag a slider on.
modules.teach: Each lab is a single-purpose calculator or visualizer, not a course. Run the numbers for a workload you actually care about — your own model size, your own context length — rather than the defaults; that's where the intuition actually lands.

labs.title: What breaks first, and at what scale?
Watch context turn into inference memory
Can you fit the workload without changing the task?
See what the model actually reads

modules.title: AI and research labs
modules.objective: Use the remaining eight labs to inspect an agent's configuration, an eval's statistical confidence, an optimizer's path, memory architectures, notation, retrieval chunking, a PDF's RAG-readiness, and your own day.
modules.teach: A few of these are directly useful outside any course: the eval-confidence lab turns a raw pass rate into a proper Wilson interval before you trust a benchmark claim, and the PDF-to-RAG scan will save you from shipping a retrieval pipeline on a badly-parsed document.
